In 2016, the IRS sent out 2.8 million notices to taxpayers for tax issues that did not require an audit. In 2017, it was 3.2 million. It seems that the agency has found new ways to do more work with fewer auditors.
The following are some tips to help you comply with the tax laws, and potentially avoid an IRS audit.
1. Report all of your income.
2. Keep thorough records.
3. If you’re self-employed, keep track of your expenses. You may be able to deduct some business-related expenses.
4. Don’t take too many deductions. Some taxpayers may be tempted to stretch the truth on their tax return, but it’s best to be honest and only claim legitimate deductions. If the IRS does come knocking, you could be hit with penalties and interest for any deductions you claimed that aren’t legitimate.
5. Don’t overclaim on your refund.
6. Don’t forget to report foreign accounts and investments. If you have any assets or accounts outside the U.S., you must report them. The penalties for not doing so can be hefty.
7. Don’t take too many charitable deductions. Many taxpayers make the mistake of overestimating their charitable deductions, so if you’re not sure of the actual amount you’re entitled to, be conservative in your estimates.
8. Don’t overlook capital gains. Don’t forget to report capital gains or losses. If you’re selling a business or other large asset, the capital gains or losses could be significant.
9. Don’t neglect to file a return if you don’t owe taxes. Even if you don’t owe taxes, you still need to file a return. Failure to do so could result in penalties.
10. Be honest and thorough when completing your tax return. If you have any questions, it’s always a good idea to consult a tax professional.
